user_story: As a user, I want the app to estimate my remaining time from my birth date and model inputs so the countdown is deterministic and inspectable.
expected_behavior: A valid birth date produces a valid estimate with age, death date, remaining milliseconds, progress from 0 to 1, and one of calm/finite/near/borrowed states. Invalid dates return an invalid estimate without crashing.
notes: Uses population life expectancy as a reflective model, not individual prediction.

user_story: As a user who moved countries, I want birth country, current country, and move age to influence the model without pretending to be clinical.
expected_behavior: Different birth/current countries blend toward the current residence after move age; no blend is applied before move age or when countries match.
notes: Model intentionally coarse; city-level effects are out of scope.

user_story: As a user, I want simple checkbox rows for sex, sleep, exercise, drinking, smoking, and health so I can make the model less generic.
expected_behavior: Each factor behaves as a mutually exclusive row, unchecked rows are skipped internally, and selected values change life expectancy by documented local offsets.

user_story: As a user, I want every main countdown surface to include seconds so the widget feels alive and precise enough for the concept.
expected_behavior: Full readouts include years, days, hours, minutes, and seconds; borrowed time is prefixed with plus.
notes: The product still labels estimates as approximate.

user_story: As a Linux bar user, I want a tiny JSON emitter so Waybar can display the countdown with classes, tooltip, and progress.
expected_behavior: Emitter loads a config or sample defaults, outputs compact JSON with text, tooltip, class array, and percentage, and includes the full disclaimer in tooltip/sample config.

user_story: As a product reviewer, I want Linux, macOS, and W11 tray previews so the primary widget can be compared across OS conventions.
expected_behavior: Workbench shows Linux system tray, macOS status menu bar, and W11 system tray with only the MM widget and system clock, with progress integrated in the widget.
notes: No adjacent fake shell items such as Finder, Start, Search, or Activities.

user_story: As a user, I want one right-click menu action to toggle between bone/ash and onyx palettes without nested settings.
expected_behavior: All three preview menus plus the live context menu expose one palette toggle; toggling updates the document skin and all palette buttons consistently.
notes: Visible labels remain bone and ash / onyx; internal skin IDs stay system-light/system-dark.

user_story: As a user, I want the full panel to minimize back into the tray widget and restore on double click so the app behaves like a tray utility.
expected_behavior: Clicking Minimize hides the panel and shows the dock widget; double-clicking the dock widget restores the panel; double-clicking panel chrome minimizes unless editing controls are targeted.
notes: Settings live inside the maximized panel.

user_story: As a non-technical user, I want one visible setup panel with no tabs or generated backend config so changing inputs recalculates immediately.
expected_behavior: Birth date, birth country, living country, since age, and checkbox rows are visible in one panel; edits update countdown/death date/model age without a restart button.
notes: Quickstart/custom split and restart clock remain removed.

user_story: As a user, I want occasional dry reminders that time is finite without titles or medical shame.
expected_behavior: Reflection copy has no popup title, uses gently acidic prompts, adapts late-night pool for late hours, and renders at minimized widget width.

user_story: As a buyer/reviewer, I want the UI to feel stylish and specific rather than generic boilerplate.
expected_behavior: Workbench uses bone/ash and onyx/gold palettes, hourglass/bone/candle motifs, Fraunces for display moments, Geist for UI, and system fallbacks.
notes: External font loading is progressive enhancement; fallbacks remain defined.

user_story: As a co-developer, I want localhost preview to load reliably after updates so iteration is not interrupted by zombie server responses.
expected_behavior: npm run serve uses the Node static server, binds to 127.0.0.1, exposes /__health, disables cache, and serves explicit HTML/CSS/JS content types.

user_story: As a tester, I want clear per-OS install paths for beta executables and source builds so I can try the product on real machines.
expected_behavior: Docs identify Linux source/Waybar as production-testable now and macOS/W11/iOS as planned beta installer/native targets; commercial model keeps beta artifacts free on GitHub Releases first.
notes: No support entitlement; Apache-2.0 source remains forkable.

user_story: As a reader, I want the philosophical justification and safety boundaries documented so the product tone is coherent and not irresponsible.
expected_behavior: README links philosophy; docs explain memento mori purpose, dry tone boundaries, classical motifs, approximate model status, and open-source commercial posture.
notes: The joke targets procrastination/self-deception, not illness or mortality itself.
